instruction: Add a comment, "Thank you so much!", to all the venmo payments I received from my roommates in the last 10 days (including today), and like those payments.
notes: Two apps (phone, venmo) plus supervisor. The supervisor profile provides the phone number (phone username) and email (venmo username); passwords come from show_account_passwords. phone.search_contacts (query=relationship='roommate') is a single call whose effect (roommates-found) unlocks the roommate emails; venmo.show_transactions is called once per roommate (user_email, direction='received', min_created_at = today - 9 days = 2023-05-24, requiring the current datetime lookup) and unlocks the transaction ids of that roommate. Like and comment actions are only applicable to transactions that are received-from a roommate AND in-window (the API's date filter), and each can be applied at most once per transaction so no duplicate likes/comments are produced. The problem uses placeholder world structure: two roommates, three in-window received payments (txn-a1, txn-a2, txn-b1) and one out-of-window distractor (txn-a0) that must remain untouched; real counts/ids are read from the API responses. Because the number of payments is instance-specific and quantified goals are disallowed, supervisor-complete-task carries the three handled payment records and the comment text as non-API (task-record) parameters so that its precondition is exactly the goal's like/comment conditions; it is the only action producing (task-completed) and every other action requires (not (task-completed)), so it is always last. complete_task is called with no answer (status success).
